newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ plans to fully dismantle national post monopoly.
newsitem.headline: NZ plans to fully dismantle national post monopoly.

text.p: New Zealand launched a bill on Tuesday intended to make the country's postal market fully open to competition by allowing new postal operators, and even allowing a range of carriers to issue stamps.

According to a copy of The Postal Services Bill, which had its first reading in parliament during Tuesday's session, the proposals would remove all restrictions on the types of post operators may carry and on the terms and conditions of carriage.
The bill "abolishes the sole right of New Zealand Post to carry letters weighing 200 grammes or less, and for which the postal charge is NZ$ 0.80 or less".
The ministry later explained that this was the last sector of the market not already open to competition, as heavier items, international services and private boxes are already freed.

The planned rules would make it possible for new operators to have the right to issue stamps bearing the words "New Zealand", or an appropriate abbreviation, while binding them to national regulations on handling and security.

A cap would be imposed on New Zealand Post, currently the only 'basic letter' carrier in the country, so that it could not raise its current NZ$0.40 letter rate above 45 cents for three years. Current service levels would also have to be guaranteed, the ministry added in a briefing document.
